model_output.cross_horizon_summary: No defensible net directional edge is established for 12h or 168h. The 72h outlook is MIXED specifically because BTC has stronger demand support than ETH and broad altcoins, not because broad recovery is confirmed. The latest final BTC ETF inflow materially improves the older structural prior's negative-flow context, but ETH outflows, weak participation and contracting short-window stablecoin supply remain counterweights. Small hourly gains indicate stabilization only; relative altcoin outperformance during declines is not recovery. These are non-binding forecasts with no portfolio execution authority.
global_missing_evidence: The supplied packet lacks a sustained multi-hour or daily price, volume and open-interest sequence; one completed hour cannot establish continuation or reversal.
Canonical large-cap and broad-alt breadth remain UNCONFIRMED. Capitalization buckets are Top-100 proxies, the small-alt bucket covers only the Top-100 tail, and microcaps are unavailable.
Only one latest final ETF session is supplied alongside older structural aggregates; persistence of the changed BTC flow picture is unknown.
BTC dominance is one settled daily observation, not an intraday reading or a supplied trend.
Stablecoin supply is observed, but deployment into risk assets is NOT_ESTABLISHED.
Catalyst context is degraded, and macro observations are dated October 16 without a supplied movement sequence. These limitations reduce visibility rather than constitute bearish evidence.
Hourly funding-event rates are null, although live-anchor funding snapshots are available. Cross-venue confirmation and liquidation evidence are not supplied.

contradicting_evidence: A rebound case has tangible support: spot taker-buy shares are approximately 55.5% for BTC and ETH, sampled taker imbalances are positive, and BTC's sampled depth imbalance is strongly positive.

A downside-continuation case also remains credible: only 27 of 100 breadth constituents advance, BTC is down 1.63% over 24h, ETH is down 2.20%, and all observed alt-capitalization buckets have negative average returns.
12h.expected_path: A stabilization or modest rebound attempt may continue, but the evidence does not establish its durability or the net 12h direction. BTC has more visible support than ETH; renewed selling remains credible. The small completed-hour gains are not sufficient evidence of recovery.
falsification_conditions: Persistent spot-led BTC and ETH gains accompanied by improving ETH/BTC and broader positive participation would replace the no-edge assessment with an upward case.
Persistent price declines, worsening participation and failure of the current buying interest to support prices would establish a clearer downward case.
missing_evidence: Follow-through after the latest completed hour and persistence of the sampled order-book and taker imbalances.
Whether rising open interest reflects durable demand or leverage vulnerable to reversal.
supporting_evidence: The latest hour shows BTC up 0.071%, ETH up 0.129% and ETH/BTC up 0.068%, contrasting with negative 24h returns rather than establishing a sustained turn.
Final settled ETF flows diverge sharply: BTC +$526.7 million versus ETH -$103.3 million, preventing a uniform demand interpretation.
BTC and ETH both show PRICE_UP_OI_UP, while long/short ratios are 1.84 and 2.46; the small rebound is therefore not demonstrably spot-only.

contradicting_evidence: The positive final BTC ETF session and moderate 90d altcoin outperformance provide a plausible constructive branch if demand persists and broadens.
Weak current participation, a 30d altseason score of 29 and declining weekly stablecoin supply provide a plausible renewed-downside branch.
168h.expected_path: There is no supported weekly endpoint. Selective BTC resilience could remain isolated, broaden into recovery, or fail into renewed weakness. Resolving those branches requires repeated flow, relative-strength and participation evidence; neither a cycle transition nor its timing is established.
falsification_conditions: Repeated positive demand evidence accompanied by sustained BTC and ETH gains, stronger ETH/BTC and broad positive participation would establish an upward weekly edge.
Persistent price weakness accompanied by continued ETH outflows, weak participation and failure of BTC demand support would establish a downward weekly edge.
missing_evidence: Several subsequent settled ETF sessions and repeated breadth and ETH/BTC observations.
A stablecoin supply trajectory showing whether weekly contraction persists, plus evidence of actual deployment.
Updated macro and catalyst evidence relevant to the forecast window.
supporting_evidence: Altseason context is horizon-dependent: the 30d score is 29, while 90d scores are 55 and 58. Neither historical window establishes next-week direction.
Stablecoin supply is nearly flat over 30d at +0.069% but down over 1d and 7d, leaving no demonstrated sustained liquidity expansion.
One strong BTC ETF session improves BTC's demand picture without establishing persistence or resolving negative ETH flows and weak current breadth.

contradicting_evidence: Broadly negative participation and negative returns across all observed alt buckets could overwhelm BTC-specific support and produce a more synchronized decline.
The Top-100 tail proxy outperforms BTC relatively, and ETH/BTC improved in the latest hour; persistent follow-through could broaden stabilization. Neither observation currently establishes recovery.
72h.expected_path: Uneven stabilization and retests are more supportable than synchronized expansion: BTC benefits from improved settled demand, while ETH and broad alt proxies remain vulnerable to failed rebounds. MIXED denotes cross-asset divergence, not a confident aggregate rise or fall.
falsification_conditions: Sustained BTC and ETH recovery with stronger ETH/BTC, broader positive participation and improving ETH flows would invalidate the divergent outlook toward broad upside.
BTC losing resilience alongside persistent ETH and altcoin weakness would invalidate divergence toward broad downside.
missing_evidence: Whether BTC ETF inflows repeat and whether ETH outflows ease.
Repeated observations demonstrating that relative altcoin resilience becomes positive absolute participation.
A supplied ETH/BTC sequence confirming more than the latest hourly uptick.
supporting_evidence: The latest final ETF session supports BTC selectively: +$526.7 million for BTC against -$103.3 million for ETH.
Large-, mid- and small-alt proxy equal-weight returns are approximately -2.10%, -1.93% and -1.04%; their advancing shares remain only 17%, 22% and 29%.
Stablecoin supply fell 0.29% over 1d and 0.77% over 7d, with deployment unconfirmed, limiting evidence for broad fresh demand.
Although 62 of 100 constituents outperform BTC, only 27 advance. Relative resilience in a declining market does not confirm positive transmission.
